headline: Solar marketing agency in Gurgaon: who buys rooftop solar and how to reach them
card_text: Gurugram's kothis, builder floors, societies and factories each buy solar differently. Here's who decides, what they need to hear and which channels reach them.
intro:
A solar marketing agency in Gurgaon has a harder job than one selling solar in a single-type city. Gurugram has old DLF and Sushant Lok kothis, builder floors in Palam Vihar and South City, high-rise societies along Golf Course Extension Road and Dwarka Expressway, villages turning into rental hubs, and factories in Udyog Vihar and Manesar. Each of these buyers asks different questions, and most of them can't say yes on their own.

This guide breaks down who actually buys rooftop solar in Gurugram, what each group needs to hear, and which channels reach them. It's written for installers, EPCs and dealers who serve Gurugram, and it's how we think about the city when we plan campaigns for the 30+ solar EPCs and manufacturers we work with.

sections.h2: Who buys rooftop solar in Gurugram
sections.html:
Before you pick a channel, split the city into the buyer types you can actually serve. In Gurugram there are five that matter:

BuyerWhere you find themWho decidesWhat they care about
Independent house ownersDLF Phases 1–5, Sushant Lok, South City, Nirvana Country, sector plotsThe owner, often with familyBill savings, roof space, brand of panels and inverter
Builder floor ownersPalam Vihar, sector plots, New GurugramThe top-floor owner, plus other floor owners for roof rightsShared roof, NOC from other floors, small systems
Housing societies and RWAsGolf Course Road, Golf Course Extension Road, Sohna Road, Dwarka Expressway, New Gurugram sectorsRWA committee, then the general bodyCommon-area bills, DG and maintenance costs, a fair proposal
Landlords with rental floorsUrbanised villages and older sectorsThe landlordPayback, lower common bills, less hassle
Factories and commercial unitsUdyog Vihar, IMT Manesar, Sector 37, Sohna beltOwner, plant head or financePayback period, capex vs RESCO, downtime during install

Most installers try to talk to all five with one ad. That's why their Gurugram leads look cheap and close badly. Pick one or two groups for your first 90 days and build everything around them.

sections.h2: Gurugram facts your marketing has to get right
sections.html:
Homeowners in Gurugram compare quotes and ask sharp questions. Your ads, website and sales calls should be accurate on these local points:

  • DISCOM: Gurugram is served by Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam (DHBVN). Net-metering applications, load enhancement and meter changes go through DHBVN, so explain those steps in plain words and say who handles the paperwork.
  • Central subsidy: under PM Surya Ghar, residential consumers can get central financial assistance of up to ₹78,000 for a system of 3 kW or more, for eligible households. RWAs and group housing societies get support for common facilities at a different per-kW rate. Check pmsuryaghar.gov.in for the current amounts before every campaign.
  • State support: Haryana has announced extra help for some groups, such as state financial assistance for Antyodaya families and interest-free assistance for certain consumers. These change, so never put a state figure in an ad without checking the current order from the Haryana renewable energy department or DHBVN.
  • Building rules: Haryana has required solar on many new buildings, including residential plots above a size threshold. That gives you a reason to talk to builders and plot owners who are constructing now. Check the current notification before quoting it.
  • Sanctioned load: a residential system generally can't be larger than the sanctioned load on the connection. Many Gurugram homes need a load enhancement first, and your team should say so on the first call.

Never write "free solar" or promise a subsidy amount as guaranteed. Say what the scheme currently offers and that eligibility depends on official rules. Our guide to PM Surya Ghar subsidy ads has wording that stays accurate.

sections.h2: What a solar marketing agency in Gurgaon should do differently
sections.html:
A generic Delhi NCR campaign treats Gurugram as one location pin. A good Gurugram plan doesn't. This is how we approach the city as a solar marketing agency serving all of NCR:

  1. Targets by sector, not the whole city. Location targeting on Meta and Google should be built from the sectors and pincodes your team can reach in a day. DLF Phase 2 and Sector 95 are both Gurugram, but they're different buyers and often different install teams.
  2. Uses both spellings. People still search "Gurgaon" as often as "Gurugram". Your Google Ads keywords, website headings and Google Business Profile description should use both naturally.
  3. Speaks to the roof situation. Ads for kothi owners show full rooftops and larger systems. Ads for builder floors talk about shared roofs and small systems. Ads for societies talk about common-area bills, not personal savings.
  4. Shows local proof. Photos and short videos of installations in recognisable Gurugram areas do more than stock images. Only show sites where the customer has agreed.
  5. Plans for longer decisions. Societies and factories take weeks or months. Their campaigns need retargeting, a proposal deck and follow-up, not just a lead form.

sections.h2: The channel mix for Gurugram installers
sections.html:
Here's how the main channels usually fit each Gurugram buyer. Use it as a starting point and judge every channel on cost per site visit, not cost per lead.

For the Meta side, our step-by-step guide to Facebook ads for solar installers covers the campaign settings and lead form in detail.

Societies are where a lot of Gurugram's rooftop potential sits, and they're the slowest sale. A few things help:

  • Find the right person. The RWA president, secretary or maintenance committee usually starts the discussion. Facility managers often know the bills best.
  • Lead with common-area costs. Lifts, pumps, corridor lights and DG backup are what the committee pays for. Show what a rooftop system could offset, based on their own bills.
  • Make the proposal easy to forward. A one-page summary, a clear quote, the subsidy position stated carefully, and answers to roof waterproofing, structure and maintenance questions.
  • Expect a general body vote. Give the committee material they can share on the society WhatsApp group, and offer to attend the meeting.

Digital ads help here mainly as proof and retargeting: committee members will look you up, so your website, Google reviews and project videos need to be ready before you pitch.

sections.h2: Qualifying Gurugram leads before the site visit
sections.html:
A wasted site visit in Gurugram traffic costs your team half a day. Filter before you send anyone:

  1. Do you own the property, and is it an independent house, builder floor or society flat?
  2. For builder floors: do you have rights to the roof, or agreement from the other floor owners?
  3. What is your average monthly bill, and what is your sanctioned load?
  4. Which sector or pincode is the property in?
  5. When do you want to install?

Ask these on the lead form or in the first WhatsApp message, and ask for a photo of the latest DHBVN bill. A lead that answers all five is worth calling within minutes. One that doesn't own the roof can be politely closed.

sections.h2: What to measure in your first 90 days
sections.html:
Track every Gurugram lead in a simple sheet or CRM: date, source, sector, buyer type, called, site visit booked, quote sent and installed. Then each week look at:

  • Cost per qualified enquiry by channel and buyer type
  • Cost per site visit, which matters more than cost per lead
  • Time to first call, aiming for minutes, not hours
  • Quote-to-install rate by area, which shows which sectors to push

For reference, our rooftop campaigns run at ₹60–80 per qualified enquiry when they're working well, and solar clients at scale typically get 20–30 leads a day and 5–10 site visits a week. Your numbers will depend on your area, offer and follow-up, and no agency can promise them in advance. We work in a 90-day sprint and then move to a flexible arrangement, so you can judge the results before committing longer. You can see the kind of work involved in our solar portfolio, which covers the Solarxp website, Sungrid's Google reviews and local SEO, Skynxt Solar's video and social, and RK Solar's lead generation.

faqs: Is there a solar marketing agency in Gurgaon that only works with solar companies?

Performance and Pixel focuses on marketing for solar businesses and serves installers and EPCs across Delhi NCR, including Gurugram, from our office in Dwarka. Whoever you hire, ask for solar-specific case studies and how they measure cost per site visit.
How much does solar marketing cost in Gurugram?

It depends on your ad budget and the agency's fee. Our rooftop campaigns run at ₹60–80 per qualified enquiry when they're working well, but your cost will depend on your target sectors, offer and how quickly your team follows up.
Which DISCOM handles net metering in Gurugram?

Gurugram is served by Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam (DHBVN). Net-metering applications and load enhancement go through DHBVN, so check its current process and charges before you explain them to customers.
Can Gurugram housing societies get the PM Surya Ghar subsidy?

RWAs and group housing societies can get central support for common facilities at a per-kW rate set under the scheme. The amounts and caps can change, so check pmsuryaghar.gov.in before quoting a figure in a proposal.
Should I advertise as Gurgaon or Gurugram?
Use both. Many people still type "Gurgaon" into Google, while official documents use "Gurugram". Use both naturally in your keywords, website and Google Business Profile.
